Frontend Playwright: (1) Owner /leave shows all 3 tabs (mine/approvals/settings), Request Leave dialog submits successfully, request appears in My Leave with 'PENDING'/'CASUAL' chips + approver name; (2) Approvals tab renders 41 pending cards, owner can Approve/Reject (with note)/Request Info (with note) — all persist and remove card from approvals; (3) Settings tab lists approver dropdowns for sales/production/finance roles (owner default fallback in first option), Save Approvers works with toast; (4) Report Absence Today dialog with reason select + note submits + shows EMERGENCY chip on card; (5) Sales user's /leave shows ONLY 'My Leave' tab — no approvals/settings — RBAC verified; (6) People → Employees → Access dialog shows 'REPORTING MANAGER (FOR LEAVE APPROVALS)' dropdown with 'None (use department approver)' + all non-owner users, plus 'Approve Leave' permission toggle; (7) /calendar shows 'LEAVE (6)' filter with teal leave events; (8) /brief brief-row-on_leave + brief-count-on_leave render for owner with counter='4', clicking opens 'ON APPROVED LEAVE TODAY' modal listing Priya Nair × 4 with 'Casual until 2026-07-17' subtitle. **Bug found**: PATCH /api/users/{id} with `reporting_manager_id: null` silently no-ops due to `if inp.reporting_manager_id is not None` guard (server.py:1219). Frontend Team.js:76 sends `form.reporting_manager_id || null`, so 'None (use department approver)' selection can never CLEAR an existing RM — only overwrite it with another user. Empty string works as a workaround.

minor.issue: Setting `reporting_manager_id: null` is a no-op — server.py:1219 short-circuits on `if inp.reporting_manager_id is not None`. Frontend Team.js:76 sends `form.reporting_manager_id || null`, so selecting 'None (use department approver)' in member-manager-select cannot CLEAR a previously-set RM. Confirmed in test_null_does_not_clear. Fix: use `payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` semantics (only update fields explicitly present in the request), OR treat null as an explicit clear. Empty string works as a workaround but the UI sends null.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1219 `if inp.reporting_manager_id is not None:` is the root cause of the 'can't clear RM' bug. Fix by either (a) using Pydantic's request-body-only-fields pattern (`__fields_set__` / `exclude_unset` at deserialization) so callers can distinguish 'not provided' from 'explicit null', or (b) treat None as 'clear' since a defined-but-null value in HTTP requests conventionally means 'clear this field'. Same pattern exists for `phone` and `permissions` fields (also guarded by `is not None`), and should be reviewed for consistency.

server.py:3067-3073 brief/details on_leave lists one item per LEAVE row, not per user. If a user has 2 approved leaves overlapping today, they appear twice. Consider `db.leaves.aggregate([{$match: ...}, {$group: {_id: '$user_id', ...}}])` or a Python-side dedupe on user_id before returning.

server.py:3798 push_notification on new leave uses `push_notification(tenant, [approver_id], ...)`. If approver_id resolves to None (edge case — tenant with no owner), this pushes to a [None] list. `_resolve_leave_approver` can return (None, None) when no owner exists — the push helper should defensively drop falsy user_ids.

server.py:3853 GET /leaves/{leave_id} — access check is `lv.user_id != user.id and not _can_approve_leave(user, lv)`. This is correct for the leave feature but note that a user with `leave_approve` perm can read ANY leave in the tenant (even ones for which they are not the routed approver). This is the intended design per RBAC (leave_approve = 'can approve leave' = 'can see all leave'), but the wording in perms.js ('Approve Leave') doesn't hint at the read-all side-effect. Consider labeling it 'Approve & View All Leave' to set expectations.

The Approvals tab shows ALL pending leaves for an approver, even for the approver themselves if someone accidentally set an approver=themselves loop. `_resolve_leave_approver` doesn't guard against `approver_id == requester['id']` (though the RM setter at server.py:1221 does guard `rm != user_id` — good). Consider adding the same guard when reading from `leave_approvers` mapping so a role manager can't be routed their own leave.

rca of the issue: Reporting-manager-clear bug RCA: When the user opens People → Employees → Access, sets a Reporting Manager, saves — the RM is persisted correctly. When the user reopens the same dialog, changes the dropdown back to 'None (use department approver)' (value=''), and clicks Save Access, Team.js:76 fires `api.patch('/users/'+id, {..., reporting_manager_id: form.reporting_manager_id || null})`. Since form.reporting_manager_id is '' (empty), `'' || null` evaluates to `null`, so the payload contains `reporting_manager_id: null`. On the backend, `UserUpdateInput.reporting_manager_id: Optional[str] = None` deserializes JSON null to Python None. The subsequent guard `if inp.reporting_manager_id is not None:` at server.py:1219 evaluates FALSE (because inp.reporting_manager_id IS None), so no `updates['reporting_manager_id']` line runs. The `update_one({..., '$set': updates})` therefore never touches the RM field, and the previously-stored value remains. Reproduction: test_null_does_not_clear (PASS = bug reproduced). Mitigation: swap `form.reporting_manager_id || null` for `form.reporting_manager_id || ''` in Team.js:76 (line 81 as well for create path), OR change server.py:1219 to treat None as clear intent (best done via `if 'reporting_manager_id' in inp.__fields_set__:` or Pydantic's `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`).
